title.raw: 卷106上 地形志二上 Volume 106a Treatise 2: Terrain 1

sentences.zh: 夏書禹貢、周氏職方中畫九州，外薄四海，析其物土，制其疆域，此蓋王者之規摹也。

translations.literal: In the Xia Document Yugong and in the Zhou Offices of the Regional Controller, within they mapped the Nine Provinces; without they drew near the Four Seas, analyzed their products and soils, and fixed their boundaries—this was roughly the kingly design.
translations.idiomatic: The Yugong chapter of the Documents of Xia and the Zhou Regional Controller within charted the Nine Provinces and without pressed upon the Four Seas, sorting their products and soils and fixing their domains—such was the sovereign's blueprint.

sentences.zh: 戰國分并，秦吞海內，割裂都邑，混一華夷。

translations.literal: The Warring States divided and merged; Qin swallowed the realm within the seas, carved up capitals and districts, and unified Chinese and barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Warring States split and reunited; Qin swallowed the lands within the seas, cut apart capitals and towns, and unified Chinese and barbarian alike.

sentences.zh: 漢興，即其郡縣，因而增廣。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it took those commanderies and counties as they were and thereby expanded them.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, it kept those commanderies and counties and enlarged them further.

sentences.zh: 班固考地理，馬彪志郡國，魏世三分，晉又一統，地道所載，又其次也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu surveyed geography; Ma Biao recorded commanderies and states; the Wei age split three ways, Jin reunified—the earth's ways as recorded rank next after that.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu examined geography and Ma Biao chronicled commanderies and kingdoms; Wei split the realm three ways and Jin reunited it—what the terrestrial records contain stands one step below.

sentences.zh: 自劉淵、石勒傾覆神州，僭逆相仍，五方淆亂，隨所跨擅。

translations.literal: From Liu Yuan and Shi Le overturning the divine land, usurpations followed in succession; the five directions were tangled in disorder, each seizing wherever it could span.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yuan and Shi Le overturned the heartland, usurpers followed one after another; the five regions fell into chaos, each holding whatever territory it could seize.

sentences.zh: □□□長，更相侵食，彼此不恒，犬牙未足論，繡錯莫能比。

translations.literal: [lacuna] grew long; they devoured one another in turn; neither side held steady—dog's-teeth jaggedness hardly suffices to describe it; brocade-mismatch cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: As [text lost] wore on, they gnawed at one another; borders shifted without end—jagged as dogs' teeth, yet even that image falls short; nothing matches the tangle of brocade threads.

sentences.zh: 魏定燕趙，遂荒九服，夷翦逋偽，一國一家，遺之度外，吳蜀而已。

translations.literal: Wei pacified Yan and Zhao, then left the nine domains wild; barbarians were cut down and fugitive usurpers—each state and house cast beyond the pale; only Wu and Shu remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei secured Yan and Zhao, the nine domains beyond lay waste; barbarians were cut down and rebel regimes swept away—every other state and house was cast outside the pale, and only Wu and Shu remained.

sentences.zh: 正光已前，時惟全盛，戶口之數，比夫晉之太康，倍而已矣。

translations.literal: Before Zhengguang the age was wholly flourishing; the count of households and mouths compared to Jin's Taikang—doubled, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Zhengguang era the realm was at its height; registered households and population were simply twice those of Jin's Taikang reign.

translations.literal: At the time of Xiaochang disorder and separation were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang years chaos and displacement were at their worst.

translations.literal: North of Heng and Dai all became ruins;
translations.idiomatic: North of Heng and Dai everything lay in ruins;

translations.literal: West of the Xiao and Tong passes, hearth-fires ceased entirely;
translations.idiomatic: West of the Xiao and Tong passes, not a hearth-fire remained;

translations.literal: In Qi the land of Zhao was whole; the dead like tangled hemp.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi and across Zhao the dead lay thick as tangled hemp.

sentences.zh: 於是生民耗減，且將大半。

translations.literal: Thus the living people dwindled, nearly half gone.
translations.idiomatic: The common people dwindled until nearly half were gone.

sentences.zh: 永安末年，胡賊入洛，官司文簿，散棄者多，往時編戶，全無追訪。

translations.literal: In the last years of Yong'an barbarian rebels entered Luoyang; official documents were widely scattered and abandoned; former registered households could not be traced at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Yong'an, barbarian raiders entered Luoyang; government registers were scattered and lost in great numbers, and the old household rolls could no longer be traced.

sentences.zh: 今錄武定之世以為志焉。

translations.literal: Now we record the Wuding era as this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Here we record the Wuding era as this treatise.

sentences.zh: 州郡創改，隨而注之，不知則闕。

translations.literal: Where provinces and commanderies were newly created or changed, we note them accordingly; what is unknown is left blank.
translations.idiomatic: Where provinces and commanderies were newly created or renamed, we note it as we go; what is unknown is left blank.

translations.literal: Interior Secretaries and chancellors continued from dynasty to dynasty in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The offices of Interior Secretary and Chancellor continued in succession from one dynasty to the next.

sentences.zh: 魏自明、莊，寇難紛糾，攻伐既廣，啟土逾眾，王公錫社，一地累封，不可備舉，故總以為郡。

translations.literal: From Ming and Zhuang of Wei, bandit troubles tangled; campaigns grew wide and new lands ever more numerous; kings and dukes were granted fiefs—one place piled with enfeoffments, too many to list in full, so they are summed as commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Ming and Emperor Zhuang of Wei onward, raids and wars multiplied; as conquests spread and new territories opened, princes and nobles received fiefs—one tract heaped with multiple grants, too many to enumerate—so they are grouped here as commanderies.

sentences.zh: 其淪陷諸州戶，據永熙綰籍，無者不錄焉。

translations.literal: Households of the fallen provinces are entered from the Yongxi bound registers; where there are none, they are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Households of the lost provinces are taken from the Yongxi bound registers; where no figures exist, none are entered.

translations.literal: 〈Seat at Ye city; Emperor Wu of Wei made his state here.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Administered from Ye; Cao Cao established his state here.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxing the Taizu established Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxing (401) the Taizu established Xiangzhou.

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping the capital was moved and the name changed.〉
translations.idiomatic: Renamed when the capital moved in the first year of Tianping (534).〉

sentences.zh: 領郡十二 縣六十五

translations.literal: It oversees twelve commanderies and sixty-five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed twelve commanderies and sixty-five counties.

sentences.zh: 戶三十七萬一千六百七十五 口一百四十五萬九千八百三十五
〈故魏郡，漢高祖置，二漢屬冀州，晉屬司州，天興中屬相州。

translations.literal: 〈Former Wei Commandery, established by Han Gaozu; in the Two Han it belonged to Jizhou, in Jin to Sizhou, in Tianxing to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Former Wei Commandery, set up by Han Gaozu; under the Two Han it belonged to Jizhou, under Jin to Sizhou, and in the Tianxing era to Xiangzhou.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it was changed to Intendant.〉
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianping it was made an Intendancy.〉

sentences.zh: 戶一十二萬二千六百一十三 口四十三萬八千二十四
〈二漢、晉屬，天平初併蕩陰、安陽，屬之蕩陰。

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin it belonged; at the beginning of Tianping it merged Tangyin and Anyang, attaching them to Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin it belonged here; at the start of Tianping it absorbed Tangyin and Anyang, which were attached to Tangyin.

translations.literal: In Taihe a pass was established; now abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A pass was set up in the Taihe era; it has since been abolished.

sentences.zh: 有西門豹祠、武城、牖里城、蕩城、[1]石竇堰。

translations.literal: There are the shrine of Ximen Bao, Wucheng, Youli city, Dang city, [1] the Shidou weir.
translations.idiomatic: Sites include the shrine of Ximen Bao, Wucheng, Youli city, Dang city, and [1] the Shidou weir.

translations.literal: There are the southern, right, and western commandants.
translations.idiomatic: It had southern, right, and western commandants.

sentences.zh: [2]天平中，決漳水為萬金渠，今世號天平渠。〉

translations.literal: [2] In Tianping the Zhang River was diverted for the Wanjin canal; today it is called the Tianping canal.〉
translations.idiomatic: [2] In the Tianping era the Zhang was cut to form the Wanjin Canal, known today as the Tianping Canal.〉

sentences.zh: 〈天平初分鄴併內黃、斥丘、肥鄉置。

translations.literal: 〈At the beginning of Tianping it was split from Ye, merging Neihuang, Chiqu, and Feixiang to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established at the start of Tianping by splitting off from Ye and absorbing Neihuang, Chiqu, and Feixiang.

sentences.zh: 有鼓山、肥鄉城、邯鄲城、斥丘城、列人城、鸕鷀陂、林臺澤。

translations.literal: There are Drum Mountain, Feixiang city, Handan city, Chiqu city, Lieren city, the Cormorant Marsh, and Lintai marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Sites include Drum Mountain, Feixiang city, Handan city, Chiqu city, Lieren city, the Cormorant Marsh, and Lintai marsh.

translations.literal: There are the left, eastern, and northern commandants.〉
translations.idiomatic: It had left, eastern, and northern commandants.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged; under Jin it belonged to Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged here; under Jin to Dunqiu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 真君六年併頓丘，太和十九年復。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenjun it was merged into Dunqiu; in the nineteenth year of Taihe it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenjun (445) it was merged into Dunqiu; in the nineteenth year of Taihe (495) it was restored.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping it belonged; seat at Fanyang city.〉
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping (535) it was attached here, with its seat at Fanyang city.〉

sentences.zh: 〈前漢屬廣平，後漢屬，[3]晉屬廣平。

translations.literal: 〈Under Former Han it belonged to Guangping; under Later Han it belonged [3] under Jin to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Former Han it belonged to Guangping; under Later Han it belonged here; [3] under Jin to Guangping.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it belonged.〉
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping it was attached here.〉

sentences.zh: 〈太和二十一年分魏置，永安元年置郡。

translations.literal: 〈In the twenty-first year of Taihe it was split from Wei to establish; in the first year of Yong'an a commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Split off from Wei in the twenty-first year of Taihe (497); a commandery was set up in the first year of Yong'an (528).

translations.literal: In Tianping the commandery was abolished and it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era the commandery was abolished and the county restored.

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged; under Jin to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged here; under Jin to Guangping Commandery.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it belonged.〉
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping it was attached here.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under Jin it belonged to Guangping; in the sixth year of Zhenjun it was merged into Ye.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Jin it belonged to Guangping; in the sixth year of Zhenjun (445) it was merged into Ye.

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe it was restored to belong.〉
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taihe (497) it was restored.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin it belonged.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin it belonged here.〉

translations.literal: 〈In the second year of Tianping it was split from Yuancheng to establish.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the second year of Tianping (535) by splitting off from Yuancheng.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged to the Zhao kingdom; under Jin to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to the kingdom of Zhao; under Jin to Guangping Commandery.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping it was attached here.

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged; under Jin to Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han it belonged here; under Jin to Yangping Commandery.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping it was attached here.

sentences.zh: 〈前漢屬廣平，後漢屬鉅鹿，晉屬廣平。

translations.literal: 〈Under Former Han to Guangping; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Former Han to Guangping; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin to Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 真君三年併列人，太和二十年復。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun it was merged into Lieren; in the twentieth year of Taihe it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun (442) it was merged into Lieren; in the twentieth year of Taihe (496) it was restored.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping it belonged.〉
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping it was attached here.〉

translations.literal: 〈In the second year of Tianping it was split from Guantao to establish; seat at Zhao city.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the second year of Tianping (535) by splitting off from Guantao, with its seat at Zhao city.

translations.literal: There is an Eastern Gentlemen-of-the-Household General in residence.
translations.idiomatic: An Eastern Gentlemen-of-the-Household General was stationed here.

translations.literal: There are Kongling city and Guan city.〉
translations.idiomatic: It had Kongling city and Guan city.〉

sentences.zh: 〈魏文帝黃初二年分魏置，治館陶城。〉

translations.literal: 〈In the second year of Huangchu Emperor Wen of Wei split it from Wei to establish; seat at Guantao city.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the second year of Huangchu (221) when Emperor Wen of Wei split it from Wei Commandery, with its seat at Guantao city.〉

sentences.zh: 戶四萬七千四百四十四 口一十六萬二千七十五
〈漢武帝為平干國，宣帝改為廣平國。

translations.literal: 〈Emperor Wu of Han made it the Pinggan kingdom; Emperor Xuan changed it to the Guangping kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han Emperor Wu made it the kingdom of Pinggan; Emperor Xuan renamed it the kingdom of Guangping.

translations.literal: In Jianwu of Later Han it was abolished and belonged to Julu.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in the Jianwu era of Later Han and placed under Julu.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年復，改治曲梁城。〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu Emperor Wen of Wei restored it and moved the seat to Quliang city.〉
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the second year of Huangchu (221) by Emperor Wen of Wei, with its seat moved to Quliang city.〉

sentences.zh: 戶二萬三千七百五十 口一十萬三千四百三

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to Wei Commandery; under Jin it belonged; seat at Ping'en city.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to Wei Commandery; under Jin it belonged here, with its seat at Ping'en city.

translations.literal: 〈In Jingming it was split from Ping'en to establish; seat at Qu'an city.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the Jingming era by splitting off from Ping'en, with its seat at Qu'an city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to the Zhao kingdom; under Jin it belonged; later to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to the kingdom of Zhao; under Jin it belonged here; later to Wei Commandery.

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenjun it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenjun (445) it was attached here.

sentences.zh: 〈前漢屬，後漢屬鉅鹿，晉屬，後罷。

translations.literal: 〈Under Former Han it belonged; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin it belonged; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Former Han it belonged here; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin it belonged here; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年復，治廣平城。〉

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe it was restored; seat at Guangping city.〉
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the twentieth year of Taihe (496), with its seat at Guangping city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under Former Han it belonged; under Later Han to Wei; under Jin it belonged.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Former Han it belonged here; under Later Han to Wei Commandery; under Jin it belonged here.〉

sentences.zh: 〈前漢屬，後漢屬鉅鹿，晉屬，永嘉後廢。

translations.literal: 〈Under Former Han it belonged; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin it belonged; after Yongjia it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Former Han it belonged here; under Later Han to Julu; under Jin it belonged here; abolished after the Yongjia era.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年復，治廣年城。〉

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe it was restored; seat at Guangnian city.〉
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the twentieth year of Taihe (496), with its seat at Guangnian city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Established by Emperor Wu of Jin; seat at Fangtou.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established by Jin Emperor Wu, with its seat at Fangtou.〉

sentences.zh: 戶二萬九千八百八十三 口一十萬二千九百九十七
〈孝昌中分南修武置，治清陽城。

translations.literal: 〈In Xiaochang it was split from Southern Xiuwu to establish; seat at Qingyang city.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the Xiaochang era by splitting off from Southern Xiuwu, with its seat at Qingyang city.

sentences.zh: 有清陽泉、馬泉、[7]丁公神、育河、陶河、熨斗泉、覆釜山、五里泉、七里熨、馬鳴泉、重泉、郡戒、[8]安陽城。〉

translations.literal: There are the Qingyang spring, Ma spring, [7] Lord Ding spirit, Yu River, Tao River, Iron spring, Overturned Cauldron Mountain, Five-li spring, Seven-li Iron, Horse-neigh spring, Double spring, commandery warning, [8] and Anyang city.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sites include the Qingyang spring, Ma spring, [7] the spirit of Lord Ding, the Yu and Tao rivers, Iron spring, Overturned Cauldron Mountain, Five-li spring, Seven-li Iron, Horse-neigh spring, Double spring, the commandery warning stone, [8] and Anyang city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei Commandery; under Jin it belonged here.

translations.literal: There are Huang family [site], Wu city, and Yiyang city.〉
translations.idiomatic: It had the Huang family settlement, Wu city, and Yiyang city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged here; later abolished.

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe it was restored; seat at Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the twelfth year of Taihe (488), with its seat at Ji city.

translations.literal: There are the tomb of Bi Gan, the temple of the Grand Duke, and Chen city.
translations.idiomatic: Sites include the tomb of Bi Gan, the temple of the Grand Duke, and Chen city.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，恒農人率戶歸國，仍置義州於城中。〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe the people of Hengnong led their households back to the state, and Yizhou was still established within the city.〉
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe (540) the people of Hengnong led their households back to the realm, and Yizhou was again set up within the city.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei Commandery; under Jin it belonged here.

sentences.zh: 有朝歌城、崔方城、大方山、淇水、白溝水、天井溝、苑城、新城、伏羲祠。〉

translations.literal: There are Chaoge city, Cuifang city, Dafang Mountain, Qi River, Baigou water, Tianjing ditch, Yuan city, Xincheng, and the shrine of Fuxi.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sites include Chaoge city, Cuifang city, Dafang Mountain, the Qi River, Baigou water, Tianjing ditch, Yuan city, Xincheng, and the shrine of Fuxi.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin to Henei; later it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han and Jin to Henei; later it belonged here.

sentences.zh: 有沁陽城、南、北二武陽城。

translations.literal: There are Qinyang city and the southern and northern Wuyang cities.
translations.idiomatic: It had Qinyang city and the southern and northern Wuyang cities.

sentences.zh: 孝景二年置郡，初治共城，後移治山陽城，尋罷。〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojing a commandery was established; at first the seat was at Gong city, later moved to Shanyang city, then soon abolished.〉
translations.idiomatic: A commandery was set up in the second year of Emperor Jing of Han (155 BCE), first seated at Gong city, later moved to Shanyang city, and soon abolished.〉

translations.literal: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the Two Han to Henei; under Jin it belonged here; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 太和二十三年復，治新洛城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe it was restored; seat at Xinluo city.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the twenty-third year of Taihe (499), with its seat at Xinluo city.

sentences.zh: 〈太和十一年立，尋罷，孝昌中復。〉

translations.literal: 〈Established in the eleventh year of Taihe; soon abolished; restored in Xiaochang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established in the eleventh year of Taihe (487); soon abolished; restored in the Xiaochang era.〉

sentences.zh: 戶一萬三千二百六十二 口五萬五千八百九十七

translations.literal: 〈Under Later Han to Julu; under Jin to Anping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Later Han to Julu; under Jin to Anping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 中興中，立南、北廣宗，尋罷，後屬。

translations.literal: In the Zhongxing era Southern and Northern Guangzong were established; soon abolished; later it belonged.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhongxing era Southern and Northern Guangzong were set up, then soon abolished; later it belonged here.

sentences.zh: 有廣宗城、建始城、建德城。〉

translations.literal: There are Guangzong city, Jianshi city, and Jiande city.〉
translations.idiomatic: It had Guangzong city, Jianshi city, and Jiande city.〉

sentences.zh: 〈真君三年併信都，太和二十二年復。

translations.literal: 〈In the third year of Zhenjun it was merged into Xindu; in the twenty-second year of Taihe it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Merged into Xindu in the third year of Zhenjun (442); restored in the twenty-second year of Taihe (498).

translations.literal: 〈Under Later Han and Jin to Anping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under Later Han and Jin to Anping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 真君二年併南宮，後復屬。〉

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenjun it was merged into Nangong; later restored to belong.〉
translations.idiomatic: Merged into Nangong in the second year of Zhenjun (441); later restored here.〉

translations.literal: 〈Established under Qin; seat at Huatai city.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Established under the Qin, with its seat at Huatai city.

translations.literal: Under Jin it was changed to Puyang; later restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin it was renamed Puyang, then later restored.

sentences.zh: 天興中置兗州，太和十八年改。〉

translations.literal: In Tianxing Yanzhou was established; in the eighteenth year of Taihe it was changed.〉
